title: Loop the join
summary: The slips live at the seams between sections. Loop the seams until they feel like nothing happened.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four even beats, the exact length of the seam between two sections: the last two beats of one section and the first two of the next, looped again and again until it feels like nothing happened.

steps.title: Loop the join
steps.body:
Where do the slips happen? Almost never in the middle of a section. They happen at the joins: the bar where one section ends and the next begins. You practised each section, but never the seam between them.

1. Find the joins in your piece: the last two beats of one section and the first two of the next.
2. Play only that seam, four beats in all, slowly, three times.
3. Loop it: play the seam again and again without stopping, five times, like a record that skips.
4. Now play the whole piece once through and listen for the joins. They should feel like nothing happened.

This works because fingers learn transitions the same way they learn notes: by repeating them. A loop gives the seam more repetitions in one minute than a full play-through gives it in a week.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: mark the joins in pencil, play each seam three times slowly
Sitting 2: loop each seam five times without stopping, then once through
Sitting 3: loops again, one notch faster on the metronome, then once through
Sitting 4: the whole piece once through twice, listening only for the joins
An old piece played once; notice where its joins are

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Slips stay in.

extras.title: Change the mood
extras.body:
1. Play the piece as if it were sad: slower, softer, every note a little longer.
2. Play it sleepy: even slower, and let the loud bars stay quiet.
3. Play it in a hurry: faster, lighter, but keep the beat steady.

What to notice: the same notes make three different pieces, and one of the moods makes the joins easiest.
